newsitem.title: USA: Immigration raid embarrasses Utah senator.
newsitem.headline: Immigration raid embarrasses Utah senator.

text.p: Utah Sen. Bob Bennett, who has often called for a crackdown on illegal immigration, said he was "embarrassed" to learn one of his businesses employed undocumented workers, a newspaper reported Wednesday.
A surprise roundup last month of undocumented Mexican nationals working in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, included a raid at Inn On The Creek, a luxury bed and breakfast owned by Bennett.
"It's a little embarassing," the Utah Republican told the Salt Lake Tribune. "Obviously the Inn On The Creek will be more careful in the future, I assure you."

The Aug. 25 raid netted 153 suspected illegal immigrants, the largest such sweep in Wyoming history, according to the Immigration and Naturalisation Service. Bennett, who learned of it when contacted Tuesday by the newspaper, said he did not know how many undocumented workers were employed at his inn.
The senator, one of the wealthiest members of the Senate with an estimated fortune of $27 million, is the sole owner of the inn and a Jackson theatre.

A trustee from the Robert S. Bennett Managed Asset Trust manages the inn, a remodeled historic mansion with rooms that rent from $149 to $380 a day, the newspaper said. In compliance with Senate ethics rules, the trust operates Bennett's holdings, the senator told the newspaper.
